controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by KELT-10; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured colour.
controls.notes: No image or colour of KELT-10 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the colour of kelt-10's light, as its colour dataset measures it.

charts.alt: The orbits of KELT-10's planets in this map from above, to scale, with KELT-10 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

KELT-10 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (67, 94, 104) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 269217040, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, moved 4 minutes earlier to where TESS measures the dip, inside the published ephemeris's 3-sigma uncertainty of 5 minutes at these dates, then averaged in 15-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Kuhn et al. 2016 (2016MNRAS.459.4281K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Kuhn et al. 2016, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2016MNRAS.459.4281K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from Kuhn et al. 2016 (2016MNRAS.459.4281K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
